llm.summary: This is a coherent writing and image-generation skill, but it needs Review because it can fetch arbitrary URLs and use an under-disclosed local RedFox API key file.

dimensions.detail: Network access is purpose-aligned but broad: fetch_article.py accepts any http/https URL, generate_image.py downloads reference URLs and sends prompts/reference images to redfox.hk, and both URL download paths disable TLS certificate verification.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is disclosed as adding the skill directory and configuring REDFOX_API_KEY; there is no installer, package install step, service registration, or startup hook.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill uses broad natural-language triggers and automatic mode inference for actions that may fetch webpages, read Skill files, call external services, and write output files, without clear confirmation boundaries.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence or privilege escalation was found, but generate_image.py falls back to reading ~/.qoder/apis/redfox.json for an API key, which is local credential/profile access not disclosed in SKILL.md or the READMEs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, article workflows, local scripts, output files, and RedFox image generation mostly fit together for an operations-content creation skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the skill making outbound requests to user-provided sites and redfox.hk. Avoid internal/private URLs and confidential unpublished content, use a sandboxed workspace, and remove or disable the ~/.qoder/apis/redfox.json fallback if you want every RedFox API key use to be explicit.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The full-pipeline claim is broad, but the artifacts do provide an LLM workflow plus scripts for URL fetching, image planning, image generation, and validation; this is not evidence of tool poisoning or malicious purpose mismatch.
[P6] unexpected: The matched 'return prompt' code returns the user-supplied image prompt after optional style handling; I found no instruction or code that extracts system or developer prompts.
[SQP-2] expected: Outbound fetching and RedFox image API use are expected for link rewriting and illustration, but the documentation under-discloses what may be fetched, uploaded, or sent externally.
[SQP-1] expected: Natural-language triggering is normal for this kind of skill, but the triggers cover network and file-output behavior without explicit mode selection or consent prompts.
[LP3] unexpected: The concern is partially supported: the skill lacks explicit permission boundaries, URL allowlists, private-address blocking, and disclosure of the home-directory API key fallback.
[SDI-2] expected: Fetching a target site for Skill promotion is purpose-aligned, but targetSiteUrl is not scoped to trusted domains or otherwise constrained.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-language defaults and templates are visible and coherent with the published materials; this is a locale limitation to disclose, not a security finding by itself.
